stem: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term *weak* acid.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The $pK_a$ values of four acids are listed below.

| acid | structural formula | $pK_a$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ | 4.8 |
| 2 | $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ | 4.9 |
| 3 | $\text{CH}_3\text{CHClCO}_2\text{H}$ | 2.8 |
| 4 | $\text{CH}_2\text{ClCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ | 4.0 |
parts.text: State the mathematical relationship between $pK_a$ and the acid dissociation constant $K_a$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
With reference to acidity, explain the difference in $pK_a$ values between

- acid 1 and acid 2,

- acid 2 and acid 3,

- acid 3 and acid 4.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Draw a fully labelled diagram of the equipment needed to measure the voltage of an electrochemical cell consisting of the standard hydrogen electrode and the standard $\text{Cu}/\text{Cu}^{2+}$ electrode.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: For the cell drawn in **(i)**, calculate the $E^\ominus_{\text{cell}}$ and state which electrode is positive.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: A monobasic acid, **D**, has $K_a = 1.23 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.
parts.text: Calculate the pH of a $0.100 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of **D**.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
An electrochemical cell similar to the one you have drawn in **(c)(i)** was set up using a $0.100 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of **D** in the hydrogen electrode instead of the standard solution.

Use the data and the Nernst equation, $E = E^\ominus + 0.059\log[\text{H}^+(\text{aq})]$, to calculate the new $E_{\text{cell}}$ in this experiment.
